13152-the-firm-of-girdlestone.title: The Firm Of Girdlestone
13152-the-firm-of-girdlestone.creator: Unknown
13152-the-firm-of-girdlestone.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The approach to the offices of Girdlestone and Co. was not a very dignified one, nor would the uninitiated who traversed it form any conception of the commercial prosperity of the firm in question. Close to the corner of a broad and busy street, within a couple of hundred yards of Fenchurch Street Station, a narrow doorway opens into a long whitewashed passage.

arxiv-2111-08427.title: Dimerization induced mobility edges and multiple reentrant localization transitions in non-Hermitian quasicrystals
arxiv-2111-08427.creator: Wenqian Han, Longwen Zhou
arxiv-2111-08427.description: Abstract Non-Hermitian effects could create rich dynamical and topological phase structures. In this work, we show that the collaboration between lattice dimerization and non-Hermiticity could generally bring about mobility edges and multiple localization transitions in one-dimensional quasicrystals. Non-Hermitian extensions of the Aubry-André-Harper (AAH) model with staggered onsite potential and dimerized hopping amplitudes are introduced to demonstrate our results.

arxiv-2203-13599.title: Learning Relational Rules from Rewards
arxiv-2203-13599.description: Abstract Humans perceive the world in terms of objects and relations between them. In fact, for any given pair of objects, there is a myriad of relations that apply to them. How does the cognitive system learn which relations are useful to characterize the task at hand?

arxiv-2208-07658.title: DRAGON: Decentralized Fault Tolerance in Edge Federations
arxiv-2208-07658.creator: Shreshth Tuli, Giuliano Casale and Nicholas R. Jennings
arxiv-2208-07658.description: Abstract Edge Federation is a new computing paradigm that seamlessly interconnects the resources of multiple edge service providers. A key challenge in such systems is the deployment of latency-critical and AI based resource-intensive applications in constrained devices. To address this challenge, we propose a novel memory-efficient deep learning based model, namely generative optimization networks (GON).

arxiv-2210-00146.title: FAST-LIO, Then Bayesian ICP, Then GTSFM
arxiv-2210-00146.creator: Jerred Chen, Xiangcheng Hu, Shicong Ma, Jianhao Jiao, Ming Liu, Frank Dellaert
arxiv-2210-00146.description: Abstract For the Hilti Challenge 2022, we created two systems, one building upon the other. The first system is FL2BIPS which utilizes the iEKF algorithm FAST-LIO2 and Bayesian ICP PoseSLAM, whereas the second system is GTSFM, a structure from motion pipeline with factor graph backend optimization powered by GTSAM.

arxiv-2212-09288.title: Effect of Bose-Einstein condensation on the viscosity of a hot pion gas
arxiv-2212-09288.creator: Kshitish Kumar Pradhan, Dushmanta Sahu, Captain R. Singh, Raghunath Sahoo
arxiv-2212-09288.description: Abstract Pion condensation in an ultra-relativistic collision is an open puzzle yet to be verified experimentally. However, it is not trivial to have a conclusive result of pion condensation due to various experimental constraints. Nevertheless, numerous theoretical approaches can help in understanding the high-temperature Bose-Einstein condensation (BEC) in a better way.

arxiv-2307-12782.title: Giant Impact Events for Protoplanets: Energetics of Atmospheric Erosion by Head-on Collision
arxiv-2307-12782.creator: Kenji Kurosaki, Shu-ichiro Inutsuka
arxiv-2307-12782.description: Abstract Numerous exoplanets with masses ranging from Earth to Neptune and radii larger than Earth have been found through observations. These planets possess atmospheres that range in mass fractions from 1% to 30%, reflecting the diversity of atmospheric mass fractions. Such diversities are supposed to be caused by differences in the formation processes or evolution.

arxiv-2310-11057.title: Mutations of noncommutative crepant resolutions in geometric invariant theory
arxiv-2310-11057.creator: Wahei Hara, Yuki Hirano
arxiv-2310-11057.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Wahei Hara, Yuki Hirano. Let X X be a generic quasi-symmetric representation of a connected reductive group G G . The GIT quotient stack 𝔛 = [ X ss ​ ( ℓ ) / G ] \mathfrak{X}=[X^{\rm ss}(\ell)/G] with respect to a generic ℓ \ell is a (stacky) crepant resolution of the affine quotient X / G X/G , and it is derived equivalent to a noncommutative crepant resolution (=NCCR) of X / G X/G .

arxiv-2312-12951.title: The Core-shift of Sagittarius A* as a Discriminant between Disk and Jet Emission Models with millimeter-VLBI
arxiv-2312-12951.creator: R. Fraga-Encinas, M. Mościbrodzka, H. Falcke
arxiv-2312-12951.description: Abstract Context. The nature of the emission region around Sagittarius A* (Sgr A* ), the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center, remains under debate. A prediction of jet models is that a frequency-dependent shift in the position of the radio core (core-shift) of active galactic nucleii (AGN) occurs when observing emission dominated by a highly collimated relativistic outflow. Aims.

arxiv-2401-05743.title: Consistent Query Answering for Existential Rules with Closed Predicates
arxiv-2401-05743.creator: Lorenzo Marconi marconi@diag.uniroma1.it, Riccardo Rosati rosati@diag.uniroma1.it
arxiv-2401-05743.description: Abstract Consistent Query Answering (CQA) is an inconsistency-tolerant approach to data access in knowledge bases and databases. The goal of CQA is to provide meaningful (consistent) answers to queries even in the presence of inconsistent information, e.g. a database whose data conflict with meta-data (typically the database integrity constraints).

arxiv-2403-11951.title: Displacement Field Analysis via Optimal Transport: Multi-Tracer Approach to Cosmological Reconstruction
arxiv-2403-11951.creator: Farnik Nikakhtar, Ravi K. Sheth, Nikhil Padmanabhan, Bruno Lévy, Roya Mohayaee
arxiv-2403-11951.description: Abstract We demonstrate the effectiveness of one of the many multi-tracer analyses enabled by Optimal Transport (OT) reconstruction. Leveraging a semi-discrete OT algorithm, we determine the displacements between initial and observed positions of biased tracers and the remaining matter field.

arxiv-2405-05974.title: Symbolic construction of the chemical Jacobian of quasi-steady state (QSS) chemistries for Exascale computing platforms
arxiv-2405-05974.creator: Malik Hassanaly, Nicholas T. Wimer, Anne Felden, Lucas Esclapez, Julia Ream, Marc T. Henry de Frahan, Jon Rood, Marc Day
arxiv-2405-05974.description: Abstract The Quasi-Steady State Approximation (QSSA) can be an effective tool for reducing the size and stiffness of chemical mechanisms for implementation in computational reacting flow solvers. However, for many applications, the resulting model still requires implicit methods for efficient time integration.

arxiv-2503-13592.title: Evolution of Massive Red Galaxies in Clusters from z = 1.0 z=1.0 to z = 0.3 z=0.3
arxiv-2503-13592.creator: Yen-Ting Lin, Kai-Feng Chen, Tsung-Chi Chen, Chen-Yu Chuang, Masamune Oguri
arxiv-2503-13592.description: Abstract A critical issue in studying the evolution of galaxy clusters is to find ways that enable meaningful comparisons of clusters observed at different redshifts, as well as in various stages of their growth. Studies in the past have typically suffered from uncertainties in cluster mass estimates due to the scatter between cluster observables and mass.

arxiv-2504-17894.title: DCT-Shield: A Robust Frequency Domain Defense against Malicious Image Editing
arxiv-2504-17894.creator: Aniruddha Bala, Rohit Chowdhury, Rohan Jaiswal, Siddharth Roheda
arxiv-2504-17894.description: Abstract Advancements in diffusion models have enabled effortless image editing via text prompts, raising concerns about image security. Attackers with access to user images can exploit these tools for malicious edits. Recent defenses attempt to protect images by adding a limited noise in the pixel space to disrupt the functioning of diffusion-based editing models.

plos-pone-0003155.description: PLOS ONE research article. Caffeine stimulates calcium-induced calcium release (CICR) in many cell types. In neurons, caffeine stimulates CICR presynaptically and thus modulates neurotransmitter release. Using the whole-cell patch-clamp technique we found that caffeine (20 mM) reversibly increased the freq

plos-pone-0004741.title: Reality = Relevance? Insights from Spontaneous Modulations of the Brain's Default Network when Telling Apart Reality from Fiction
plos-pone-0004741.creator: Anna Abraham, D. Yves von Cramon
plos-pone-0004741.description: PLOS ONE research article. Although human beings regularly experience fictional worlds through activities such as reading novels and watching movies, little is known about what mechanisms underlie our implicit knowledge of the distinction between reality and fiction. The first neuroimaging study to address

pmc-10484442.title: Drug dosage modifications in 24 million in-patient prescriptions covering eight years: A Danish population-wide study of polypharmacy
pmc-10484442.creator: Cristina Leal Rodríguez, Amalie Dahl Haue, Gianluca Mazzoni, Robert Eriksson, Jorge Hernansanz Biel, Lisa Cantwell, David Westergaard, Kirstine G. Belling, Søren Brunak, Benjamin P. Geisler, Laura Sbaffi, Benjamin P. Geisler, Laura Sbaffi

To address this aspect of polypharmacy, the objective of the present study was to identify co-medications associated with more frequent dosage adjustments. The data foundation was electronic health records from 3.

pmc-11359004.title: Dhurrin in Sorghum: Biosynthesis, Regulation, Biological Function and Challenges for Animal Production
pmc-11359004.creator: Bo Wang, Wangdan Xiong, Yanjun Guo, Ros Gleadow
pmc-11359004.description: Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) holds a significant position as the fifth most vital cereal crop globally. Its drought resistance and robust biomass production, coupled with commendable nutritional value, make sorghum a promising choice for animal feed. Nevertheless, the utilization of sorghum in animal production faces hurdles of dhurrin (a cyanogenic glycoside) poisoning.

pmc-11535181.title: miR-320b, a Future Expected New Biomarker for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Induces Dysglycemia by Targeting PTEN
pmc-11535181.creator: Jinxingyi Wang, Ruyu Tao, Hanshuai Hu, Jiejie Gao, Yang Liu, Jie Xia, Xue Lan, Yanan Di
pmc-11535181.description: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has emerged as a global epidemic issue, with high rates of disability and fatality. Traditional diagnostic biomarkers are typically detected once a metabolic imbalance has already occurred, thus the development of early diagnostic biomarkers is crucial for T2DM. Metabolomics studies have identified several predictive biomarkers for T2DM, including miR-320.

pmc-11599095.title: PANoptosis Regulation in Reservoir Hosts of Zoonotic Viruses
pmc-11599095.creator: Anantika Chandra, Sannula Kesavardhana
pmc-11599095.description: Zoonotic viruses originating from reservoir hosts, such as bats and birds, often cause severe illness and outbreaks amongst humans. Upon zoonotic virus transmission, infected cells mount innate immune responses that include the activation of programmed cell death pathways to recruit innate immune cells to the site of infection and eliminate viral replication niches.

pmc-12568122.title: Deciphering the Role of Macrophages in RSV Infection and Disease
pmc-12568122.creator: Sara Van Looy, Axelle Fransen, Lotte Jacobs, Sofie Schaerlaekens, Martina Ceconi, Francisco I Serrano-Cano, Noor Ul Hudda, Laurence Van Moll, Marie De Smedt, Paul Cos, Peter L Delputte, Theo J Moraes
pmc-12568122.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe respiratory infections in infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised persons. Innate immune responses to RSV, which are crucial for containment of the infection yet may also be linked to severe disease, are well-studied in the main RSV target cells, respiratory epithelial cells, but the role of pulmonary macrophages (MΦs), key innate immune regulators, remains incompletely defined.

pmc-12655394.title: Biological Activities of Novel Kombuchas Based on Alternative Ingredients to Replace Tea Leaves
pmc-12655394.creator: Noemi Hontana-Moreno, Diego Morales, Sabina Lachowicz-Wiśniewska
pmc-12655394.description: Background/Objectives: Traditional kombucha is produced by fermenting a sweetened infusion of Camellia sinensis leaves with a symbiotic consortium of bacteria and yeasts (SCOBY). The growing interest in this beverage has driven the exploration of alternative substrates, including a wide range of plant-based raw materials, such as leaves, fruits, flowers, and seeds.

pmc-12717449.title: Range Modeling and Surveillance of Ornithodoros turicata Ticks: Implications for Detecting African Swine Fever Virus in the United States
pmc-12717449.creator: Christopher J. Butler, Cora P. Garcia, Alexa K. Mendoza, Leila Akhand, Isaac Neuman, Dee B. Ellis, Meriam N. Saleh
pmc-12717449.description: African Swine Fever virus (ASFv) is a re‐emerging global swine disease that, if introduced to the United States, would cause severe economic consequences. The widespread presence of feral hogs in addition to the presence of competent tick vectors, specifically Ornithodoros turicata , fosters a greater risk of ASFv establishment.

pmc-12739940.title: Antidiabetic Activity of Moringa oleifera Aqueous Leaf Extract on Prediabetic Wistar Male Rats
pmc-12739940.creator: Titing Nurhayati, Vita Murniati Tarawan, Happy Delia, Faisal Faisal, Hanna Goenawan, Setiawan Setiawan
pmc-12739940.description: PurposeDiabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic disorder linked to sedentary lifestyles, which reduces insulin sensitivity and increases hyperglycemia risk. Standard treatments include lifestyle changes and medications. Recently, herbal remedies like Moringa oleifera leaves have gained attention due to bioactive compounds—polyphenols and flavonoids—believed to have antihyperglycemic effects. However, research on their impact on prediabetic conditions remains limited.

pmc-12775023.title: Investigation of image-guided in vivo irradiation on voiding patterns and bladder contractility in female mice
pmc-12775023.creator: Sarah McDowell, Conor Breen, Niamh McKerr, Kirtiman Srivastava, Daniel Crummey, Mihaela Ghita-Pettigrew, Karl T Butterworth, Joe M O’Sullivan, Kevin M Prise, Karen D McCloskey
pmc-12775023.description: Radiotherapy for pelvic malignancies impacts the bladder causing urinary symptoms in many patients. Preclinical models using image-guided irradiation enable investigation of the physiology underlying radiation-response in the bladder. We aimed to characterise voiding patterns and bladder contractility following image-guided irradiation of the mouse bladder.

pmc-13386792.creator: Anja Helmer, Alexia Clavier, Maria Arnold, Adrian Segiser, Heidi E. L. Lischer, Selianne Graf, Mojgan Masoodi, Georgia Beer, Rahel Ottersberg, Manuel Egle, Matthias Siepe, Sarah Longnus

pmc-13688753.creator: Boyu Song, Rui Dong, Tingting Liu, Xu Yang, Zhili Zhang, Haixia Feng
pmc-13688753.description: AimsThis study aimed to investigate the expression, clinical significance, and underlying molecular mechanism of miR-34a-5p in Lumbar disc herniation (LDH).MethodsA total of 112 patients with LDH and 112 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum miR-34a-5p expression was measured by RT-qPCR, and its diagnostic value was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.
